title: Record Shop, Redskin Rhumba and Sally, Irene and Mary: his brief acting career
summary: Barnet says his acting was only sideline bandleading, and that sideline musicians rank lowest with directors.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Uh-uh. Uh-uh. 'Record Shop,' 1957, 15 minutes. Universal music featurette with Ella Mae Morse, the Lancers, Tex Williams, Alfan Copeland, plus Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra. Remember that?
That was one of those short subjects.
It doesn't say Will Cowan, but it doesn't say who it was. It doesn't say what you played either, so --
Well, it was undoubtedly Will Cowan, because he did all of those things there.
And then here's one that does say Will Cowan, 1948, 15 minutes, 'Redskin Rhumba,' Universal International featurette spotlighting Charlie Barnet and His
Orchestra, in a garden setting, supported by Clark Dennis and Virginia Maxie, vocalists. Numbers, "Redskin Rhumba," "Skyliner," --
That's who that blond in that picture is, Virginia Maxie, yeah.
"Jeepers Creepers," "Peg o' My Heart," and, "Jealousy." So that's -- the band in the photograph is the band from "Redskin Rhumba." It says in a garden setting and --

In a garden setting, okay. And "Sally, Irene and Mary," which you mentioned, 1938. The musical with only average songs and dances adapted from a Broadway success and featuring Charlie Barnet in an acting role.
There again it's the sideline bit, standing there, waving your arms.
That's interesting, because I found references in a bunch of books to your brief career as an actor.
Which implied that you were doing, you know, dramatic roles, but the only dramatic roles you did was as bandleader.
Well, that could be dramatic, right?
Well, hardly. There's nothing lower on the totem pole with a director than a sideline musician.
